title: Reproduction package for: A Heterogeneous Graph Framework with Multi-Level Contrastive Learning for Primary SOC Classification in the MedDRA Multi-Parent DAG
description:
Reproduction code and experimental artefacts for a manuscript submitted to the Journal of Biomedical Informatics (JBI).

The method embeds MedDRA terms by combining term-name semantics (PubMedBERT) with the five-level multi-parent hierarchy, using a heterogeneous graph encoder and a multi-level weighted contrastive loss with positive-negative mutual exclusion.

Contents

  • 01_code/ — graph construction, training (SAGE / GAT / noGNN), inductive variants, seed re-runs, attribution diagnosis, and three external baselines (text embedding, knowledge-graph embedding, graph self-supervision).
  • 02_data_dictionary/ — field specification for the flat input table, plus a fully synthetic demo dataset and its generator, so the pipeline can be exercised without a MedDRA licence.
  • 04_results/ — consolidated result tables.
  • 05_resource_ledger/ — parameters, memory, peak GPU memory and per-epoch time for 22 configurations.
  • 06_split_verification/ — evidence that every run shares one identical train/validation/test split (verified member-by-member).
  • 07_run_artifacts/ — per-run metrics, training histories, joint-subgroup diagnosis output, baseline results and provenance records. Every number reported in the manuscript traces to these files.

MedDRA data are NOT included. MedDRA is distributed by the MSSO under its own licence and must not be redistributed. Academic users must obtain a subscription or MSSO approval; commercial users must purchase a licence. The synthetic demo dataset is provided precisely so that the code path can be verified without a licence.

Environment used for the reported results: Ubuntu 22.04, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.0 (see requirements.txt).
